title: Task validity in financial synthetic data
markdown:
## 1 Distributional fit and task validity Modern tabular generators address different distributional problems. [CTGAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503) handles mixed discrete and continuous data, multimodality, and class imbalance through mode-specific normalization and conditional vectors, and [TabDDPM](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html) runs Gaussian diffusion on numerical fields and multinomial diffusion on categorical ones ([CTGAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503); [TabDDPM](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html)). Both can learn empirical distributions effectively. A financial task can match its distribution and still be invalid, though, because part of what makes it valid is structural. Accounting identities have to hold exactly, fiscal periods have to run in chronological order, covenant applicability conditions have to be respected, and the numerical inputs have to agree logically with the reference judgment. Global distributional similarity metrics cannot enforce any of this. A simple construction shows how far apart the two can drift. Suppose valid financial inputs $`x \in \mathbb{R}^d`$ have to satisfy $`m`$ linear accounting or ratio identities $`Ax = b`$, where $`A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d}`$ has full row rank, so that the valid population distribution $`P`$ is supported entirely on the affine subspace $`M = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : Ax = b\}`$. Assume this distribution has finite second moments, and let the columns of $`N \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times m}`$ form an orthonormal basis for the normal space orthogonal to $`M`$. Now take a generator that captures $`P`$ along the manifold but adds a small amount of independent noise in the normal directions: $`X_\sigma = X + \sigma N \varepsilon`$, where $`\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_m)`$ is independent of $`X \sim P`$. Writing $`Q_\sigma`$ for the generated distribution, I obtain, for every $`\sigma > 0`$, $$ W_2(P, Q_\sigma) \le \sqrt{E\|X_\sigma - X\|^2} = \sigma \sqrt{m} \longrightarrow 0 \quad (\text{as } \sigma \to 0^+) $$ $$ P(M) = 1, \qquad Q_\sigma(M) = 0 $$ $$ \|P - Q_\sigma\|_{\text{TV}} := \sup_B |P(B) - Q_\sigma(B)| = 1 $$ The first line comes from coupling $`(X, X_\sigma)`$ on the same probability space. The second holds because $`AN`$ is invertible and a continuous $`m`$-dimensional Gaussian vector equals zero with probability zero, and taking the Borel set $`B = M`$ then gives the third. So the 2-Wasserstein distance $`W_2(P, Q_\sigma)`$ can tend to zero while the acceptance rate under exact business constraints stays at zero ($`Q_\sigma(M) = 0`$) and the total variation distance stays at its maximum value of $`1`$. With a numerical tolerance the acceptance rate depends on the ratio of tolerance to off-manifold noise, and Section 2 shows that at a fixed ratio it falls geometrically with each added constraint. This counterexample motivates how I divided responsibilities in the synthetic data architecture ([SDV constraint-augmented generation](https://docs.sdv.dev/sdv/modeling/constraint-augmented-generation-cag)): • Copula models and conditional sampling capture cross-sectional rank and tail dependencies among continuous corporate indicators, including company size, operating history, leverage, and profit margins. They preserve the dependencies that independent column generation would discard. • [CTGAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503) and [TabDDPM](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html) model mixed-type and multimodal empirical distributions, and explicit business-rule checks follow them. • Deterministic variable transformations and manifold projections enforce accounting equalities, ratio bounds, and chronological order. ## 2 Preserving the conditional distribution under business constraints Rejection sampling generates unconstrained candidates and discards those that violate the constraints, and as several financial constraints tighten its computational cost can become prohibitive. Suppose a candidate draw produces $`m`$ standardized constraint residuals that behave as independent standard normal variables, each of which has to lie within $`[-\epsilon, \epsilon]`$. The acceptance probability and the expected number of candidate draws per valid input are $$ \alpha_m(\epsilon) = [2\Phi(\epsilon) - 1]^m \sim \left( \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \epsilon \right)^m \quad (\epsilon \to 0^+), \qquad E[N_{\text{attempts}}] = \frac{1}{\alpha_m(\epsilon)} $$ so each additional accounting or ratio constraint multiplies the expected candidate count. With a tolerance of $`\epsilon = 0.05`$ residual standard deviations, the exact analytical values are:
Simultaneous constraints ($`m`$)Rejection-sampling acceptance rate $`\alpha_m(\epsilon)`$Expected candidate draws per valid input
**1**3.9878%25.08
**2**0.1590%628.84
**4****0.0002529%****395,442.59**
Generating directly along the degrees of freedom the constraints permit avoids these rejected draws, and in the linear Gaussian setting covariance-weighted affine projection also preserves the exact theoretical conditional distribution. For a Gaussian copula, this result requires constraints that are affine in the latent Gaussian coordinates, since nonlinear marginal transformations generally do not preserve affine constraints in the observed financial variables. Let the initial unconstrained draw be $`Z \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \Sigma)`$, with $`\Sigma \succ 0`$. To satisfy the linear constraints while preserving the theoretical conditional covariance, I apply a covariance-weighted Mahalanobis projection: $$ X = \arg\min_{x : Ax = b} \frac{1}{2}(x - Z)^\top \Sigma^{-1}(x - Z) = Z + K(b - AZ), \qquad K = \Sigma A^\top (A \Sigma A^\top)^{-1} $$ The first-order Lagrangian stationarity condition is $`\Sigma^{-1}(X - Z) + A^\top \lambda = 0`$, and substituting $`AX = b`$ and eliminating the multiplier $`\lambda`$ gives the closed-form update. Since $`AK = I_m`$, every draw satisfies $`AX = b`$ exactly. Its mean and covariance are $$ E[X] = \mu + K(b - A\mu) $$ $$ \operatorname{Cov}(X) = (I - KA)\Sigma(I - KA)^\top = \Sigma - \Sigma A^\top (A \Sigma A^\top)^{-1} A\Sigma $$ Affine transformations preserve Gaussianity, so these moments identify the exact regular conditional Gaussian distribution of $`Z \mid AZ = b`$ ([Majumdar and Majumdar on Gaussian distributions under linear conditioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.09285)). My synthetic validation benchmark generated **200,000 12-dimensional financial vectors subject to 4 simultaneous linear constraints**. The maximum absolute constraint residual was **$`1.21 \times 10^{-14}`$**, and the relative Frobenius covariance error against the theoretical conditional covariance was **0.662%**. These were direct constrained draws with no subsequent rejection; the nearly 400,000 candidate draws reported above belong to the separate standardized-residual rejection model. Fields that accounting definitions fully determine are computed analytically. Range bounds and date ordering are enforced in the latent generation space when they admit bijective transformations, such as logarithmic transforms or positive increments $`t_{k} = t_{k-1} + \exp(\xi_k)`$. ## 3 Using decision margins to determine when reference judgments need recomputation A synthetic variant of a financial reference case often keeps the business narrative and changes decisive financial figures, covenant thresholds, or macroeconomic inputs. If the original reference answer stays in place after those values change, systematic label errors enter post-training, even when all accounting constraints hold. [FinQA](https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.300/) pairs financial questions with executable reasoning programs, and synthetic preference data similarly require a maintained link between inputs, reference conclusions, and the expert's explanation of a preference ([FinQA](https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.300/)). Neighboring work links data generation to feedback in other ways. [WizardMath](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.09583v1) couples the evolution of mathematical instructions with reinforcement feedback, and [FinGPT](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.10485v1) fine-tunes financial language models on feedback from the market. I make the dependencies among a financial scenario, its reference conclusion, the evidence behind that conclusion and the expert preference built on it the object of design, so that a change to the scenario reaches each of them. Consider a decision rule that chooses between two corporate actions, and let $`d(x)`$ denote the net valuation or metric advantage of action A over action B, so that the correct reference decision is $`\operatorname{sign} d(x)`$. If $`d`$ is $`L`$-Lipschitz on a feasible neighborhood, a sufficient condition for retaining the original reference decision is that the perturbation $`\Delta`$ stays strictly within the decision margin: $$ |d(x + \Delta) - d(x)| \le L\|\Delta\|, \qquad |d(x)| > L\|\Delta\| \implies \operatorname{sign} d(x + \Delta) = \operatorname{sign} d(x) $$ This condition certifies the decision label. A loan can stay approved while the calculation behind it, the supporting evidence and the relative quality of two responses all change, so I check reference calculations, evidence and pairwise preferences separately. My diagnostic tasks focus on contested decision boundaries where models are prone to error, which means $`|d(x)|`$ is deliberately kept small. For a linear comparison rule $`d(x) = w^\top x - c`$ with initial margin $`\gamma = d(x) > 0`$, the stale-label error rate has an exact closed form. Let the perturbation within the feasible manifold satisfy $`\Delta \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Omega)`$, with projected variance $`s^2 = w^\top \Omega w > 0`$. The probability that the correct label flips while the original decision is retained is $$ \Pr\{d(x + \Delta) < 0\} = \Pr\{w^\top \Delta < -\gamma\} = \Phi\left(-\frac{\gamma}{s}\right) $$ Validation with $`1,000,000`$ Monte Carlo draws gave the following inherited-label error rates: • At a margin-to-noise ratio of $`\gamma / s = 2`$, the error rate was **2.28%**. • At $`\gamma / s = 1`$, it was **15.87%**. • Near a diagnostic decision boundary, at $`\gamma / s = 0.25`$, it was **40.13%**. I therefore tie case expansion to reference-answer recomputation and renewed five-level pairwise preference grading when perturbations approach or cross a decision boundary. In that event the workflow recomputes the reference solution and samples new candidate model reasoning trajectories. Domain experts then assess the pair on the five-level preference scale and identify which trajectory recognized the decisive variable whose change reversed the decision and supported its judgment with primary evidence. [HelpSteer2-Preference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01257) gives a comparison point from the methods literature. ## 4 Specifying the information available to each temporal task A cross-sectional company comparison does not require continuous-time stochastic processes. Dynamic tasks such as derivatives valuation, interest-rate term-structure interpolation, and liquidity stress tests over multiple periods do require path generators. For those I use SDEs and neural SDEs to model path distributions beyond single-time marginals ([Neural SDEs as Infinite-Dimensional GANs](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v139/kidger21b.html)). Brownian bridges and stochastic interpolation support conditioning on known intermediate observations or endpoints, following the constructions in [Glasserman, *Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering*, Chapter 3](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-21617-1). That conditioning can introduce temporal leakage into evaluation, and I derive the size of the effect in closed form. Consider scaled Brownian motion $`X_u = \sigma W_u`$, where $`s < t < T`$. Under squared-error loss, the optimal predictor at time $`s`$, given only the historical filtration $`\mathcal{F}_s`$, has conditional mean squared error $`\sigma^2(t - s)`$. If the generator conditions paths on the future endpoint $`X_T`$ and inadvertently exposes that conditioning to a forecasting task, Gaussian conditioning gives ([Pitman on the Brownian bridge](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~pitman/s205s03/b_bridge.pdf)): $$ \operatorname{Var}(X_t \mid \mathcal{F}_s) = \sigma^2(t - s) $$ $$ \operatorname{Var}(X_t \mid \mathcal{F}_s, X_T) = \sigma^2(t - s) - \frac{[\sigma^2(t - s)]^2}{\sigma^2(T - s)} = \sigma^2(t - s)\frac{T - t}{T - s} $$ At the midpoint $`t = (s + T)/2`$, conditioning on $`X_T`$ halves the conditional variance. The resulting **29.29% apparent reduction in RMSE** ($`1 - 1/\sqrt{2}`$) comes entirely from the additional endpoint information in this construction, and whether that counts as a flaw depends on the task. It is temporal leakage if the forecasting task does not permit access to that information. If instead the task gives the model both endpoints $`X_s`$ and $`X_T`$ and asks it to audit an interpolation or backcast an intervening accounting period, Brownian bridge conditioning is consistent with the specified information set. The task specification therefore keeps three information sets apart: 1. **Construction information ($`\mathcal{F}_{\text{gen}}`$):** the complete path, endpoint, or latent parameters used to generate a scenario. 2. **Permitted predictor filtration ($`\mathcal{F}_s`$):** the historical information the task allows the model to observe at decision time $`s`$. 3. **Evaluation and oracle information ($`\mathcal{F}_{\text{eval}}`$):** outcomes realized after $`s`$, reserved for scoring or for explicitly disclosed oracle baselines. ## 5 Batch Zero: independent execution and calibration for post-training data strategy I created **Batch Zero** around the capability objectives and data requirements of post-training research teams. Before anything scales, it brings task design, synthetic data strategy, and preference supervision under a common set of acceptance criteria. It tests whether domain experts can independently execute a research specification, reproduce reference solutions, and calibrate their preference judgments. The resulting specifications support subsequent data construction. • **Independent execution:** before a task family enters large-scale data construction (*Batch One*), doctoral-level domain experts independently write seed cases, generate synthetic variants, verify reference solutions, and assign five-level pairwise preference scores. Implicit assumptions, missing information, and ambiguities in the specification come to light this way. • **Calibration and feedback to data strategy:** failures, expert disagreements, and boundary-case errors inform revisions to task instructions, reference solutions, grading rules, and Batch One data acceptance criteria. Task design, execution, revision, and recalibration form an iterative process. • **Organizational adoption:** the partner foundation model company subsequently adopted **Batch Zero** across other post-training programs. For statistical analysis and evaluation, I treat the task family as the basic unit of effective coverage and uncertainty estimation. Suppose $`G`$ independent reference-case families each yield $`k`$ synthetic variants, giving $`Gk`$ nominal records, and any two variants within a family have correlation $`\rho`$ and common variance $`\sigma_Y^2`$. The sample mean then carries the Kish design effect $`1 + (k - 1)\rho`$, which gives the effective sample size $`N_{\text{eff}}`$: $$ \operatorname{Var}(\bar{Y}) = \frac{Gk\sigma_Y^2 + Gk(k - 1)\rho\sigma_Y^2}{(Gk)^2} = \frac{\sigma_Y^2}{Gk}[1 + (k - 1)\rho] \implies N_{\text{eff}} = \frac{Gk}{1 + (k - 1)\rho} $$ With $`G = 100`$ independent families, $`k = 20`$ variants per family ($`2,000`$ nominal tasks), and within-family correlation $`\rho = 0.5`$, the 2,000 records provide the same precision for estimating the mean as about 190 independent records. Ignoring this correlation understates standard errors by a factor of **$`3.24\times`$**. My data workflow therefore separates training and evaluation sets at the task-family level, and all confidence intervals account for hierarchical clustering at both the family and expert levels. ## 6 Staged evaluation design and coverage efficiency Staged, blinded comparisons across independent task families test whether constraint-preserving synthesis and preference supervision meet the data requirements of post-training research teams. The task mix, generator training budget, expert review budget, and final acceptance criteria stay fixed as each method is introduced:
Comparison stageMethod introducedWhat the stage measures
**Current data construction baseline**Unconstrained generation plus expert review and reworkFully loaded cost of each valid case that is ultimately accepted
**Add manifold-constrained generation**Hold the generator fixed; apply affine projections and variable transformationsChange in invalid candidates and manual repairs, with the conditional distribution preserved
**Add decision-margin checks and reference-answer recomputation**Recompute reference judgments when the sufficient Lipschitz margin condition fails; use $`\gamma/s`$ to quantify Gaussian label-flip riskChange in stale-label errors, with valid supervision on both sides of the decision boundary
**Apply Batch Zero acceptance criteria and filtration rules**Jointly check the temporal information boundaries in $`\mathcal{F}_s`$, independent execution, reproducibility of reference solutions, and calibration of preference standardsPost-training gains that persist once leakage is excluded and clustering by source task family is accounted for
Raw acceptance rates favor trivial variants of easy templates, and generation speed alone omits the cost of expert repairs, so I allocate data construction and review resources by scenario-weighted task-family coverage efficiency. Let $`j`$ index predefined cells in the financial capability matrix, with strategic weights $`w_j \ge 0`$ ($`\sum_j w_j = 1`$) and required counts of independent valid task families $`n_j^* > 0`$: $$ \operatorname{Coverage} = \sum_j w_j \min\left(1, \frac{n_j^{\text{valid}}}{n_j^*}\right), \qquad \operatorname{Efficiency} = \frac{\operatorname{Coverage}}{C_{\text{generation}} + C_{\text{review}} + C_{\text{rework}} + C_{\text{adjudication}}} $$ Once a cell reaches its target of $`n_j^*`$ independent task families, further variants of simple templates add no coverage ([Alaa et al. on synthetic data evaluation](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/alaa22a.html)). Four controls enter that efficiency: manifold constraint enforcement, decision-margin label recomputation, separation of temporal information sets, and Batch Zero calibration.
